channel.title: Joshua S. Speagle · News
channel.description: News and press from Joshua S. Speagle, astrostatistics at the University of Toronto.

item.title: Five new postdoctoral fellows and PhD students join our group at U of T
item.description: Postdoctoral fellows Christian Kragh Jespersen (Schmidt AI in Science & CITA National Fellow), Maryum Sayeed (Arts & Science Fellow), and Chloe Cheng (Research Excellence Fellow), along with doctoral students Ian Zhang and Isabelle Huang, join our research group at the University of Toronto.

item.title: Mairead Heiger completes her PhD, joins UVA as a joint GECO/CosmicAI postdoctoral fellow
item.description: Mairead Heiger successfully defended her PhD in the David A. Dunlap Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics (co-supervised with Ting Li) and joins the University of Virginia as a joint GECO and CosmicAI Postdoctoral Fellow.

item.title: Mairead Heiger and Simran Nerval win the 2026 Fieldus Award
item.description: Mairead Heiger and Simran Nerval received the department’s Fieldus Award recognizing a high level of research acumen and service. Mairead was honored for her spectroscopic follow-up of the ultra-faint dwarf galaxies Eridanus IV and Centaurus I, her galactic chemical evolution modeling framework, and her leadership as GASA co-chair.

item.title: Constraining supernova yields and delay times from dwarf spheroidal galaxies
item.description: Led by PhD student Mairead Heiger (with Ting Li and collaborators), our new study uses Bayesian chemical evolution modeling of Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies to constrain Type Ia and core-collapse supernova nucleosynthetic yields and delay-time distributions.

item.title: A deep 3-D dust map of the southern Galactic plane from DECaPS2
item.description: Co-led with Catherine Zucker and Andrew Saydjari (ApJ, 992, 39), we inferred distances and extinctions for over 550 million stars in the DECaPS2 survey using brutus to construct the deepest 3-D dust map of the southern Milky Way plane.

item.title: Steffani Grondin and Michael Poon win the 2025 Jui Lin (Allen) Yen Award
item.description: Steffani Grondin and Michael Poon received the department’s Jui Lin (Allen) Yen Award for exceptional graduate research achievement, recognizing Steffani’s doctoral thesis on white dwarf binaries, extra-tidal stars, and dynamical ejections in star clusters.

item.title: Steffani Grondin completes her PhD, joins UC San Diego as an NSERC postdoctoral fellow
item.description: Steffani Grondin successfully defended her PhD in Astronomy & Astrophysics (co-supervised with Maria Drout and Jeremy Webb) and joins UC San Diego as an NSERC Postdoctoral Fellow.

item.title: Sam Berek completes her PhD, joins UMass Amherst as an NSF postdoctoral fellow
item.description: Sam Berek successfully defended her PhD in the David A. Dunlap Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics (co-supervised with Gwen Eadie) and joins UMass Amherst as an NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellow.

item.title: ChronoFlow: an AI model for the ages of stars
item.description: Led by PhD student Phil Van-Lane (co-supervised with Gwen Eadie; ApJ, 987, 152), ChronoFlow uses conditional normalizing flows calibrated on open star clusters to infer stellar rotation-age posteriors across the Milky Way, with press coverage in U of T News and Phys.org.

item.title: First white dwarf–main-sequence binary candidates in open star clusters
item.description: Led by PhD student Steffani Grondin (ApJ, 976, 207), our team combined Gaia DR3, GALEX ultraviolet photometry, and machine learning to identify 52 post-common-envelope white dwarf–main-sequence binary candidates across 38 open star clusters, covered by U of T Arts & Science, Phys.org, and SciTechDaily.

item.title: Sam Berek and Shivan Khullar win the 2024 Jui Lin (Allen) Yen Award
item.description: Sam Berek and Shivan Khullar received the department’s Jui Lin (Allen) Yen Award. Sam was honored for her paper introducing zero-inflated Bayesian hierarchical count models (HERBAL) to model galaxy–globular cluster scaling relations.

item.title: A 5-D map of the Milky Way: AAS Nova featured image
item.description: Our lead-author study (Speagle et al. 2024, ApJ, 971, 136) mapping distances, extinctions, and stellar properties for 170 million stars across the Milky Way using brutus was highlighted as an AAS Nova Featured Image.

item.title: Students train AI for the Galaxy Zoo: Euclid citizen-science project
item.description: U of T Statistical Sciences profiled undergraduate researchers Khalid Edris and Junbo (Felix) Li, co-mentored with Dunlap Fellow Mike Walmsley, on fine-tuning the Zoobot foundation model to classify galaxy morphologies from the Euclid space telescope.

item.title: Connaught New Researcher Award
item.description: Awarded the University of Toronto’s Connaught New Researcher Award in support of early-career faculty research in astrostatistics, Bayesian inference, and survey science.

item.title: DECaPS2: a survey of 3.3 billion objects in the Milky Way's plane
item.description: The second data release of the Dark Energy Camera Plane Survey (Saydjari et al. 2023, ApJS, 264, 28) catalogued 3.32 billion objects across 6.5% of the night sky in the southern Galactic plane, with press coverage in NSF NOIRLab, Space.com, PBS NewsHour, and Salon.

item.title: 2022 John Charles Polanyi Prize in Physics
item.description: Awarded the 2022 John Charles Polanyi Prize in Physics by the Council of Ontario Universities and the Government of Ontario in recognition of early-career research in statistical astronomy and Milky Way cartography.

item.title: The Local Bubble: the Sun sits in a 1,000-light-year void that forms stars
item.description: Using 3-D dust maps and Gaia space astrometry, our Nature study (Zucker et al. 2022) showed that virtually all nearby young star-forming complexes lie on the expanding surface of the Local Bubble, covered by CfA, the Harvard Gazette, STScI, and Smithsonian Magazine.

item.title: Mapping the Milky Way: an interactive tool for 170 million stars
item.description: Profiled by the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics on developing the allsky interactive panchromatic sky visualization and mapping 170 million stars and interstellar dust across the Galaxy.

item.title: dynesty published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
item.description: The release paper for dynesty, our open-source Python package for dynamic nested sampling and Bayesian posterior and evidence estimation, appeared in MNRAS (493, 3132) and has now been cited over 2,200 times.

item.title: The Radcliffe Wave: the largest gaseous structure in the galaxy
item.description: Co-authored the Nature discovery (Alves et al. 2020) of a coherent 9,000-light-year undulation of interconnected star-forming clouds in the solar neighborhood using 3-D dust mapping with brutus, featured by CfA and the Harvard Gazette.
